root-cause the 3 failures: (1)+(2) release.core is recursively frozen (lists become tuples) by the sealed CanonicalIrRelease.create() -- two test assertions expected lists, fixed to expect tuples; (3) a genuine design bug: require_resolved_references' sealed _unique_strings helper rejects duplicate entries in the 'referenced' list, but a shared target referenced by more than one resource (a diamond reference graph) is legitimate and must not be rejected as a duplicate -- fixed by passing only the distinct set of referenced targets, never a flat list with repeats

full local pytest regression, 3 reports/tests suites

requirement_results.command: a valid corpus with declared field types and resolved cross-resource references compiles deterministically, verified via the sealed verify_deterministic_build oracle
a resource missing the field_types key, or missing a type declaration for one of its own fields, is rejected with TYPE_ERROR
a field declaring a type name outside the closed type grammar is rejected with UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY
a field value that does not satisfy its own declared type -- including a boolean value against a declared integer type, since bool is a Python subclass of int -- is rejected with TYPE_ERROR
a resource declaring more than one distinct execution owner is rejected with MULTIPLE_EXECUTION_OWNERS; a single owner repeated is correctly accepted as unambiguous
a resource referencing another resource not compiled in the same request is rejected with UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE, via the sealed require_resolved_references helper

a direct two-resource reference cycle and a longer three-resource cycle are both rejected with CONSTRAINT_ERROR, naming the cycle; a legitimate non-cyclic diamond reference graph (two resources sharing one common referenced target) compiles successfully
genuinely malformed YAML is rejected with SOURCE_INVALID, matching OCOR-DEV-0028's own parser behavior byte-for-byte
a declared id mismatch is rejected with CONSTRAINT_ERROR
a rejected compilation (a cyclic reference graph) never returns any CanonicalIrRelease object, partial or otherwise
full local pytest regression, no new failures versus the pre-existing sandbox baseline (the two known interpreter-pin failures are unrelated and pre-existing)

residual_risks: This is the first task to seal evidence under gate G4 -- reports/evidence/G4/MANIFEST.json is created fresh by this task, mirroring the schema OCOR-DEV-0028 established for the first G3 manifest.

The closed type grammar (string, integer, number, boolean, list) is deliberately minimal, matching 'the smallest contract-compliant implementation'; it is not a claim of covering every type the eventual full OAC grammar will need, only enough to prove the type-checking discipline itself (declare, satisfy, or be rejected).

The 'references' field and cycle/resolution checking are new semantic constructs this task introduces, distinct from CompilerRequest's own sealed external dependency-lock import resolution (which OCOR-DEV-0028 already exercises); both are exercised here without modifying CompilerRequest itself.

A genuine design bug was found and fixed before this evidence was sealed: require_resolved_references' sealed uniqueness check on 'referenced' would have wrongly rejected any legitimate diamond reference graph (two resources sharing one common referenced target) as a duplicate-resource error -- see the commands log above.

DiagnosticCode values NON_DETERMINISTIC_OUTPUT, ARTIFACT_DRIFT, SIGNATURE_INVALID and RELEASE_REJECTED remain out of this task's scope: NON_DETERMINISTIC_OUTPUT and RELEASE_REJECTED are already exercised structurally by the sealed verify_deterministic_build/CanonicalIrRelease.create() helpers this task reuses; ARTIFACT_DRIFT and SIGNATURE_INVALID belong to the not-yet-implemented IrSigner/ArtifactGenerator/CompatibilityChecker protocols, which remain unimplemented sealed Protocols, same as OCOR-DEV-0028 left them.
The same pre-existing local-venv gap noted in prior evidence (uv cannot resolve the exact 3.12.11 interpreter in this sandbox) is unchanged and out of this task's scope.
rollback_procedure_verified: Every test constructs a fresh CompilerRequest/FrontendCanonicalIrBuilder per test case; no shared mutable state exists between tests. Verified directly by 4 consecutive full test-suite runs with no manual cleanup between them, and by the no-partial-release-on-rejection test proving every failure path raises before any release object is ever constructed.
